question: For every positive real number $x$, let $g(x)=\lim _{r \rightarrow 0}((x+1)^{r+1}-x^{r+1})^{1/r}$. What is the limit of $g(x)/x$ as $x$ goes to infinity?

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{g(x)}{x} & =\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\lim _{r \rightarrow 0}((x+1)^{r+1}-x^{r+1})^{1 / r}}{x} \\
& =\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \lim _{r \rightarrow 0} \frac{(x+1)^{r+1}-x^{r+1}}{x^{1+r}} \\
& =\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \lim _{r \rightarrow 0} \frac{(1+\frac{1}{x})^{r+1}-1}{(1+\frac{1}{x})^{r+1}} \\
& =\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{1}{(1+\frac{1}{x})^{r+1}} \\

$$

question: what is the limit of $2/\sqrt{\pi}*\sqrt{n}\int_0^1(1-x^2)^n dx$ as n goes to infinity?
model_outputs: We have \begin{align*} \lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}} \sqrt{n} \int_{0}^{1}(1-x^{2})^{n} d x & = \lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}} \sqrt{n} \int_{0}^{1} e^{-n x^{2}} d x \\ & = \frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}} \int_{0}^{1} \lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \sqrt{n} e^{-n x^{2}} d x \\ & = \frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}} \int_{0}^{1} \lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \sqrt{n} e^{-n x^{2}} d x \\ & = \frac{2}{\sqrt{\pi}} \int_{0}^{1} 0 d x \\ & = 0 . \end{align*}The answer is (J).
